problem: Supervised and pretrained-model-based ObjectNav methods struggle to prioritize candidate frontier goals effectively at each decision step, and RL exploration training is unstable.
motivation: ObjectNav in unseen environments needs high-level reasoning about which frontier to visit combined with low-level control. Better frontier scoring that fuses semantic maps, goal text and pose, plus a reward that encourages coverage, should improve efficiency and training stability.
key_idea: Score frontier candidates with a confidence module that fuses channel- and spatial-attention over semantic maps with CLIP goal-text and pose embeddings via cross-attention, and train with an exponential coverage reward.
insight: According to the abstract, ablations show both the attention-based fusion and the exponential reward are pivotal to the gains. No specific ablation numbers are available because only the abstract was provided.
method: Channel attention: aggregates per-channel statistics over the semantic map to recalibrate feature importance
Spatial attention: highlights critical regions of the semantic map
Goal-text and pose embeddings: CLIP-based goal-text embeddings and pose embeddings are joined with the map features to guide goal selection
Cross-attention confidence module: refines the joined features and outputs confidence scores for frontier candidates
Exponential coverage reward: RL reward that promotes efficient exploration and stabilizes training

setting.backbone: attention-based confidence module with CLIP text embeddings, trained with RL
setting.training_data: not stated in abstract (RL training on ObjectNav environments)
setting.observation: semantic map, pose, goal text (details not given in abstract)

results: The abstract claims significant gains in SR and SPL over competitive baselines on standard ObjectNav benchmarks. No numbers or baseline names are given.
